chain_name: Finding 2 — investigators never put a name to the shooter
section: §ES · Executive summary, finding 2 (line 21); cross-referenced to §6 · The surrender and arrest
changed_since: An earlier, plainer form asserted flatly that law enforcement did not know the shooter's identity until Robinson surrendered, placed the arrival of the name AT the walk-in, and cited the family-recognises-the-photograph account as sworn testimony. The P7 pass of 2026-09-14 added three qualifications inside the same finding: (a) the testimonial answer is relabelled a QUALIFIED answer ('a person of interest' + 'did not specifically know who the shooter was') rather than a flat ignorance claim; (b) the name is relocated to BEFORE the walk-in, reaching investigators from Washington County roughly 30–60 minutes ahead of arrival; (c) the photograph account is re-sourced from the hearing record to the Information's sworn probable-cause statement and re-assigned to the recording layer. The bolded headline sentence 'Investigators never put a name to the shooter' was NOT itself rewritten, and the §6 section this finding cites still opens with the flattened form ('Robinson was not identified by investigators' … 'law enforcement did not know the shooter's identity until Robinson surrendered').

premises: Sworn testimony given at the preliminary hearing addresses the state of the investigation as of the evening of 2025-09-11.
That testimony states investigators had a person of interest developed from surveillance imagery.
The same testimony states investigators 'did not specifically know who the shooter was.'
implicit_premises: The witness who gave this answer was in a position to know the identification status of the whole investigation, not merely his or her own unit's or personal knowledge.
'Did not specifically know who the shooter was' means no name had been attached to the shooter, rather than meaning a name was held but not yet confirmed to the required certainty.
Having 'a person of interest developed from surveillance imagery' is not itself equivalent to having put a name to the shooter.
The evening of 2025-09-11 is the operative cut-off for the finding, i.e. nothing between the shooting and that evening produced a name.
A specific sworn locator exists for the quoted answer — §ES supplies no witness name, day, or timestamp for it.

The quoted words are accurately rendered and correctly attributed in the source transcript, notwithstanding §1 item 1's warning that Rev speaker labels are unreliable and speakers must be inferred from content.
steps.conclusion: As of the evening of 2025-09-11, investigators had a surveillance-derived person of interest but had not, on the sworn record, attached a name to the shooter.

premises: The name reached investigators from Washington County at the point when Robinson's approach was relayed.
That relay occurred roughly half an hour to an hour before Robinson arrived.
Robinson's arrival at the Washington County Sheriff's Office (the walk-in) was just before 9 p.m. on 2025-09-11.
implicit_premises: The name relayed from Washington County was Robinson's, and was accurate and actionable rather than an unverified tip.
A relay of a name from Washington County counts as 'investigators' coming into possession of the name, i.e. the receiving body is continuous with the 'investigators' of S1.

Receiving a name from an outside relay is not the same as investigators 'putting a name to' the shooter — the finding's headline survives because the name was supplied to them rather than developed by them.
The 30-to-60-minute interval and the fact of the relay rest on some sourced record; §ES states neither a source, a tier, nor a confidence grade for the interval.
No separate investigative route produced the name between the evening testimony of S1 and the relay — a null whose search scope is not stated here.
steps.conclusion: The name reached investigators before the walk-in rather than at it, arriving from outside the investigation roughly 30 to 60 minutes ahead of Robinson's arrival.

premises: The account in which family members recognise the released photograph of the suspect appears in the sworn probable-cause statement of the Information.
The Information is a charging document, not hearing testimony.
This library's standing rule places what a filing or claimant asserts in the recording layer and only independently established fact in the analyst layer.
An earlier form of this finding cited the photograph account as sworn testimony.
implicit_premises: A probable-cause statement sworn by an officer inside a charging document does not qualify as 'sworn testimony' for this project's purposes, despite also being sworn.
The layer assignment turns on the instrument type (charging document vs. hearing record) rather than on whether the underlying statement was made under oath.
The photograph account appears in no sworn hearing testimony anywhere in the five-day record — a completeness claim whose search scope is not stated in this finding.

Labelling the earlier citation as a layer error is sufficient to remove the account from the analyst layer; the finding does not restate what, if anything, the photograph account may now be used to support.
steps.conclusion: The family-recognises-the-photograph account is recording-layer material from a charging document and cannot be asserted as an analyst-layer established fact; the earlier citation of it as testimony was a layer error.

premises: What the hearing record carries is that Robinson told his immediate family he had been involved and wanted to turn himself in.
implicit_premises: The hearing record was searched for the photograph-recognition account and does not contain it, while it does contain the family-disclosure account.

This substituted proposition is itself established rather than merely alleged — it is stated as what the record 'carries', with no allegation label, no tier, no confidence grade and no citation in §ES.

The family-disclosure account is sufficient to do the work the photograph account previously did in the finding, i.e. to explain how the surrender came about without an investigator-side identification.
'Told his immediate family he had been involved' can be asserted without adopting the truth of the underlying admission, under the recording/analyst separation.
steps.conclusion: The sworn hearing record supports only that Robinson disclosed involvement to his immediate family and wished to surrender — not the photograph-recognition mechanism.

premises: Investigators held only a surveillance-derived person of interest and no name as of the evening of 2025-09-11 (S1).
The name came to them from an outside Washington County relay 30–60 minutes before the walk-in (S2).
The photograph-recognition account is recording-layer charging-document material, not sworn testimony (S3).
The sworn record carries only the family-disclosure account (S4).
implicit_premises: 'Never put a name to the shooter' is to be read as scoped to investigative work up to the moment of the outside relay, not as a claim that investigators never at any time held the name — on the finding's own S2 they did hold it, before the walk-in.

The bolded headline sentence is governed by the qualifications printed after it rather than standing as its own unqualified assertion; a caveat naming the earlier flattening does not by itself restate the headline in narrowed terms.
The two routes considered (surveillance-derived development and the outside relay) exhaust the ways investigators could have obtained the name; no third route is excluded on a stated search scope.

§6, the section cited in support, states the narrowed proposition rather than the withdrawn flattened one — the finding's parenthetical '(§6)' presupposes that the cross-referenced section carries what this finding now says.
Recording that an earlier form erred, and naming the error, is equivalent to the file no longer relying on the erroneous form anywhere in its footprint.
steps.conclusion: The finding stands in narrowed form: the identification did not come from investigative work on the surveillance imagery, but from an outside relay shortly before Robinson's voluntary surrender, and the widely repeated photograph-recognition account is a pleaded allegation rather than sworn testimony.

chain_name: The pliers: the hedge retired, and the residual relocated to the ruling
section: §8.6 · Firearms, toolmark and the inscription convergence — final bullet (line 338); cross-referenced at §12 item 7
changed_since: An earlier form characterised the bullet-jacket-manipulation question as 'a live thread carried nowhere.' The 2026-09-14 correction states both halves were wrong: the thread is not live (it was resolved under oath by the report's author in July 2026) and it was not carried nowhere (it is recorded at CR-E01 §3.2). Added since: the named witness, counsel and two transcript locators; the photographed as-received/after case-file pages at pp. 14–15 with their admission and identification timestamps; an explicit demotion of CR-ACQ-2026-07-27 §3.2 from corroboration to pointer; and a closing scope limit relocating the residual from the manipulation question to the unobtained ruling. §12 item 7 was correspondingly re-scoped so the ruling remains open while the pliers question is declared no longer an open item.

premises: The defence's 2026-01-09 ballistics motion reproduces the State's own notice.
On that notice, the ATF examiner 'may have already folded back pieces' of the bullet jacket fragment.
The motion further records that the report 'contains no hint' of any such folding back.
implicit_premises: The motion's quotation of the State's notice is faithful, and the notice's own 'may have' is the State's hedge rather than the motion's characterisation.
'Folded back pieces' and the later testimonial 'peeled the petals back' describe the same physical operation on the same fragment.

The motion's assertion that the report contains no hint of it is accurate as to the four-page report — a claim this library is positioned to check, since it holds and has read that report, but which this bullet does not state was checked.
The proposition at issue is whether the fragment was manipulated before examination and whether that manipulation was disclosed — the two limbs are not separated here.
steps.conclusion: As of the 2026-01-09 motion, whether the bullet jacket fragment had been manipulated before examination stood as a hedged, unresolved proposition.

premises: The author of that report testified under oath that she cleaned the bullet jacket fragment and peeled the petals back, and that she had to do some maneuvering of those petals.
Asked whether she used an instrument, she answered 'I use pliers.'
The testimony was given by Samantha Karner on direct examination by defence counsel Mr. Burt, who called the State's own examiner.
The locators are day4.txt at 06:39:23 and 06:39:54.
implicit_premises: The witness who testified is in fact the author of the four-page report the motion complained of — §8.6 elsewhere establishes only that she described her scope as the submission-one report, so the identity of witness and report author is an inference on this record.
A witness's in-court description of her own laboratory conduct is sufficient to establish that conduct at High confidence without this project having read the underlying report or case file.

The Rev machine transcript's rendering of the words and its attribution of them to the witness rather than to examining counsel are correct, notwithstanding §1 item 1's standing warning that answers are routinely mislabelled and speakers must be inferred from content.
The cited timestamps are recording-stream locators and are stable enough to serve as citations.
That the examiner was called by the defence rather than the State does not bear on the reliability of her answer, or bears on it only favourably.
steps.conclusion: The manipulation actually occurred, was performed by the report's author, and was performed with pliers — so the State's 'may have' hedge is retired and converted to established fact.

premises: Her case file contains an as-received image of Exhibit 6 at p. 14 and an after-examination-preparation image on the next page.
The case file was admitted into evidence over the State's Rule 403 objection at 06:36:35.
Page 14 was identified in testimony at 06:38:40 and the next page at 06:40:30.
implicit_premises: The pages identified in testimony as p. 14 and 'the next page' are pp. 14–15, i.e. the pagination is inferred from the testimony rather than read off the document.
The case-file images show what the testimony describes them as showing — this project has read only the testimony describing them, not the case file itself.
Admission over a Rule 403 objection establishes only that the exhibit is in evidence and says nothing about the accuracy or completeness of its contents.
Contemporaneous photography of a preparation step is what 'documented' requires for this purpose.
steps.conclusion: The preparation of the fragment was documented and photographed in the examiner's case file, not undocumented.

premises: The photographic documentation is located in the examiner's case file.
The four-page report the motion complained of is a distinct artifact from the case file.
implicit_premises: The case file was not attached to, incorporated into, or served with the four-page report.
Whether the case file had been disclosed to the defence at the time of the 2026-01-09 motion is not stated and is not treated as bearing on the analysis.
Documentation existing somewhere in the examiner's materials is compatible with the report itself containing no hint of the manipulation — the two are not in conflict.
steps.conclusion: The motion's specific complaint that the report contains no hint of the manipulation is not contradicted by the case-file photographs; what changes is that documentation is shown to exist elsewhere.

premises: CR-E01 §3.2 records this resolution.
CR-ACQ-2026-07-27 §3.2 is a pointer rather than independent corroboration.
That file's own row retires the hedge expressly as 'RESOLVED TO FACT 2026-07-27 (CR-E01 §3.2)', i.e. on this same testimony.
implicit_premises: An internal library row derived from the same testimony can never add corroborative weight, however many files repeat it.
No source outside the Day 4 testimony bears on the question — a null whose search scope is not stated in this bullet.
A single-sourced proposition resting on one witness's answer, mediated by an uncertified Rev machine transcript, can nonetheless carry a High confidence grade.
steps.conclusion: The entire resolution rests on one testimonial source, and the apparent second internal citation supplies no independent support.

premises: The manipulation question is resolved under oath (S2) and the preparation is shown to have been documented (S3).
This resolution strengthens the factual premise of the defence's motion.
It says nothing about whether the motion should have been granted.
The ruling on the motion was never obtained and is unheld.
implicit_premises: The motion's factual premise was that the fragment had been manipulated before examination — so confirming the manipulation strengthens the motion rather than undercutting it.

Establishing that the manipulation WAS documented and photographed does not cut against the motion's non-disclosure limb, or the two limbs are severable enough that confirmation of the first counts as strengthening overall.
A resolved factual question and an unobtained ruling are cleanly severable, so the file can declare the pliers question closed while the motion's disposition stays open (as §12 item 7 does).
Nothing else about the fragment's handling remains unresolved — the residual is the ruling and only the ruling, a scope assertion made without stating what else was checked and cleared.
Declining to assess whether the motion should have been granted is a sufficient discharge of the legal-care obligation, without any further statement of the ruling's likely effect.
steps.conclusion: The hedge is retired and the only surviving residual is the unobtained ruling on the motion, not the manipulation itself.

chain_name: Case posture: oral ruling → bindover on all seven counts → probable cause only → presumption intact
section: §ES (posture-first blockquote; "What is not established") + §11 (Case posture as of 2026-09-14 — the bindover), with the allegation-level detail at §4 and the procedural spine at §7
changed_since: The chain now runs on two artifacts rather than one: the 2026-09-01 Rev transcript AND the signed written Ruling and Order acquired 2026-09-14. premises: The source for the 2026-09-01 proceeding is a transcript of that hearing day, acquired 2026-09-14 and banked with SHA-256 hashes.
The transcript records that the court recessed to integrate 24 pages of notes taken during argument, then ruled from the bench, count by count.
No testimony was taken on 2026-09-01; that day was argument, the oral ruling, and arraignment on a closed evidentiary record.
implicit_premises: That the Rev machine transcript accurately records what the court did and said, even though the file states in the same paragraph that it is newly acquired, has not been through a verification cycle, and carries a standing hazard that speaker labels are unreliable.
That the reliability defect the library attributes to Rev renderings (speaker attribution) does not touch the content being used here — an oral ruling delivered by a single identified speaker.
That the artifact titled as the final preliminary-hearing day is a transcript of the 2026-09-01 proceeding in this case and of the whole of it.
That '24 pages of notes' and 'recessed to integrate' are on the transcript's face rather than reconstructed.
steps.conclusion: On 2026-09-01 the court delivered an oral ruling from the bench, count by count, on a closed evidentiary record.

premises: The court took each count in turn and bound Counts 1 through 6 over at the degrees charged: one capital felony, one first-degree felony, two second-degree felonies, two third-degree felonies.
The court bound Count 7 over as what it called a class B misdemeanor reclassified as a class A misdemeanor under section 76-3-203.14(3)(a)(ii).
The court then entered a single consolidated order naming every count and the sentencing allegation attaching to each.
The Information of 2025-09-16 charges seven counts.
implicit_premises: That the seven counts the court ruled on are the same seven counts of the Information — i.e. that no count was dropped, added or merged between charging and ruling.

That Count 7, described by the court as a class B reclassified to class A, is the same count §4 records as charged at class A misdemeanour — that the court's description is a statement of statutory mechanics and not a change in what was bound over.
That a consolidated order naming every count is equivalent to a bindover of every count, rather than a docketing device that could name a count without binding it over.
That the oral ruling and the later written order agree count-for-count; the file reads both and asserts no divergence, but states no comparison act.
steps.conclusion: All seven counts were bound over for trial.

premises: The court found the victim-targeting allegation satisfied the probable-cause standard but held that its legal consequence differs by count.

On Count 7 the statute reclassifies the offence; on Count 2 it makes victim selection an aggravating sentencing consideration rather than reclassifying; as to Count 1 the court declined to decide that the statute authorises an additional penalty, and preserved the State's notice.

The operative written order names for Count 1 only the capital aggravating circumstance under section 76-5-202(2)(a)(iii); it names the targeting allegation for Counts 2 and 7; and it names the presence-of-a-child factor for Count 2 only, under section 76-3-203.9.
The Information pleads the targeting enhancement on Counts 1, 2 and 7 and the presence-of-a-child factor on Counts 1 and 2.
implicit_premises: That a declination to decide a penalty consequence is not a rejection of the allegation — stated in the file as a conclusion, not derived from anything the court said about the difference.

That a count's bindover status and degree are unaffected by which sentencing allegations the order carries forward on it, so that re-sorting the allegations leaves 'all seven counts bound over' intact.

That the subsection pinpoint 76-5-202(2)(a)(iii) attaching to Count 1 in the order is the same circumstance the Information pleaded as a bare '(iii)' under an unpinpointed section — §4 states this identification is the library's own, not the Information's text.
That the written order is 'operative' over the oral ruling where the two could be read differently, a priority the file asserts by word choice and does not argue.
steps.conclusion: The ruling changed which sentencing allegations survive on which counts without changing that every count was bound over at the degree stated.

premises: The court restated on the record that the preliminary hearing's primary purpose is the ferreting out of groundless and improvident prosecutions, that the State's burden is light, that evidence is viewed in the light most favourable to the State, and that whether the State can prove the aggravating circumstance beyond a reasonable doubt remains for trial.

The written Ruling and Order states that its findings do not determine the defendant's guilt, the ultimate credibility of witnesses, the weight of the evidence, or the admissibility of evidence at trial (page 2, repeated page 25).
The same order quotes Virgin for the proposition that magistrates must leave all weighing of credible but conflicting evidence to the trier of fact (page 7).
The court's Count 1 aggravator conclusion is expressly limited to the circumstances reflected in this record and establishes no categorical rule.
implicit_premises: That the court's own statement of the standard it applied is an accurate description of the standard actually applied, so that the ruling can be characterised by the court's self-description.
That a disclaimer inside the order governs how every finding in it may be read downstream, including findings the disclaimer does not name.
That the page citations to pp. 2, 7 and 25 were read correctly off a rendered scan with no text layer, where no string search can confirm placement.
That 'probable cause only' exhausts what a bindover decides — the file elsewhere notes admissibility rulings under Rule 1102 WERE made over objection, which the same disclaimer appears to deny.
steps.conclusion: The bindover is a finding of probable cause under a deliberately low standard and adjudicates no fact as true.

premises: Arraignment followed in the same session on 2026-09-01.
Counsel waived reading of the Information and entered pleas of not guilty to all counts on the defendant's behalf, and the court found the waiver knowing and voluntary.
A bindover decides probable cause only and no court has found any fact in this document to be true.
This document records the State's allegations without adopting any of them.
implicit_premises: That a plea entered by counsel on the defendant's behalf is the defendant's plea for the purpose of stating his posture.

That 'no court has found any fact in this document to be true' is consistent with a court having just made probable-cause findings about the same material — the fact/finding distinction is assumed, never stated.

That the presumption of innocence is a legal status untouched by the volume or content of the evidence recited elsewhere in the document, so no amount of §8 forensic material qualifies the word 'absolute'.
That entering a not-guilty plea is a routine procedural step carrying no evidential weight in either direction.
steps.conclusion: The defendant stands bound over on all seven counts with not-guilty pleas entered to every one, and the presumption of innocence is intact.

premises: The ruling, the pleas and the arraignment all occurred on 2026-09-01.
A pretrial conference was set for 2026-10-23 at 1:00 p.m., chosen over an offered 24 September date on counsel availability, with trial dates to be set at that hearing.
The document is prepared as of 2026-09-14 and states the posture as of that date.
Everything else in the document depends on the posture statement.
implicit_premises: That nothing occurred between 2026-09-01 and 2026-09-14 that changed the posture — the currency of the date-stamp rests on nothing having been observed, not on an observation that nothing happened.

That this assumption survives the file's own access-path caveats: no docket coverage after 2026-03-14 is held, no minute entry from 2026-09-01 has been obtained, and a current docket requires a paywalled, owner-gated XChange account.
That one transcript plus one written order exhaust the procedural events of 2026-09-01, so no unrecorded ruling or filing that day could qualify the posture.
That scheduling a pretrial conference is itself confirmation that the case advanced to the post-bindover stage.
steps.conclusion: As of 2026-09-14 the case posture is bindover on all seven counts with not-guilty pleas, and every other section of the document is to be read against that posture.

Every bindover fact therefore came from reporting alone, and the reporting was consistent across multiple outlets.

That the pre-2026-09-14 search for the order and minute entry was wide enough to warrant 'not reachable'; the same section later concedes the decisive 2026-09-02 verification fetched at 13:08–13:12 UTC, before the court's own 24-hour filing window had run.

premises: A transcript of the 2026-09-01 final hearing day was acquired on 2026-09-14 and banked with hashes.
It is a contemporaneous record of the proceeding at which the ruling was delivered.
The library already assigns a grade to its other Rev hearing-day transcripts.

premises: The Ruling and Order on Preliminary Hearing Bindover was acquired and verified on 2026-09-14.

That the transcript's rendering of that one sentence is accurate — the transcript being the artifact the same paragraph describes as not yet verification-cycled.

That verification fetched between 13:08 and 13:12 UTC on 2026-09-02, before the court's own 24-hour window had run, and the two routes that would have settled the question were unreadable.

That the withdrawn watch-run report, whose sourcing was never established, is retroactively vindicated by a date it may merely have coincided with rather than reported.
That the timing of the 2026-09-02 fetch is the explanation for the null, rather than one candidate explanation among several.

chain_name: Activity and transfer: whose DNA it is cannot become what anyone did
section: §8.4 finding 3, with its load-bearing statements at §8.1 and §ES finding 3; supported at §9 item 2, §8.2 caution 1, §10
changed_since: §ES finding 3 now carries three narrowings the plainer earlier form did not: (a) "unqualified" is withdrawn — the FBI examiner's answer was qualified, she agreed only that she could not give the *precise* action or *exact* time; (b) the corpus-wide superlative "the single most consistent proposition in the entire body of evidence" is withdrawn as a ranking this file is not positioned to make and replaced with "the proposition on which both laboratories' analysts agreed and which no located record item contradicts"; (c) the "on the State's own examination, not only on cross" distinction is withdrawn because BOTH DNA analysts were defence witnesses, so the State's examination of each WAS the cross-examination. But §8.1 and §8.4 finding 3 still carry the pre-narrowing wording verbatim — §8.1 still says "unqualified and unrebutted by anyone" and "That is the most consistent proposition in the entire body of evidence," and §8.4 finding 3 still says the FBI analyst "described a transfer mechanism on the State's own examination." The narrowings therefore exist in §ES and have not propagated into the section that carries the chain. The steps below decompose the §8 sentences as written and record the §ES caveats where they name a gap in them.

premises: The ATF analyst and the FBI examiner each testified at the preliminary hearing about the DNA items naming Robinson.
Neither stated what action deposited any DNA on any item.
Neither stated when any DNA was deposited.
§8.4 finding 3 characterises this as the question being answered strongly in the negative by both laboratories, not merely as a gap.
§ES finding 3 records that the FBI examiner's answer was qualified: she agreed she could not give the precise action or the exact time.
steps.conclusion: On the hearing record, neither laboratory's analyst stated what action deposited DNA on any item, or when.
implicit_premises: That the questions actually put to each analyst reached the activity-level and timing propositions in a form whose negative answer settles them — "answered strongly in the negative" treats the answers as findings about what the evidence can support rather than as the boundary of what was asked.

That the FBI examiner's qualified answer (no *precise* action, no *exact* time) is equivalent in force to the unqualified form §8.1 still uses, i.e. that the qualifiers leave no room for an approximate action or an approximate time.

That the two analysts' agreement is convergent support rather than two instances of one convention — §8.4's own closing paragraph records four FBI/DOJ reporting limits that were put to the FBI examiner and confirmed followed by her, which would make the agreement a shared reporting rule rather than two independent determinations.
That an analyst's statement of what she cannot say is itself testimony about the limits of the evidence, rather than testimony about the limits of her own assignment and knowledge.

premises: Neither analyst stated what action deposited any DNA, or when.
§ES finding 3 states that no located record item contradicts that position.
No analyst attributed any DNA to Robinson as its source (§9 item 2).

Every ATF statement naming Robinson is a likelihood ratio between two hypotheses about whose DNA is in a mixture, and the FBI statements about him are either "aligned" language about mixture components or two likelihood ratios read in by a non-expert witness (§9 item 2).
steps.conclusion: The DNA results in this record carry propositions about whose DNA may be present in a mixture, and not propositions about what any person did.
implicit_premises: That what these two witnesses could not say is a limitation of DNA mixture evidence itself, not of these witnesses, their instructions, or this examination.

That the search space in which a contradicting record item would have to appear has actually been searched. §8.4 states State's Exhibit 31 and the ≥379-page FBI case file are not banked and have never been read; §9 item 7 records twelve laboratory reports unread and the two FBI DNA case files unread; §8.2 records that the faces of State's Exhibits 30 and 33 have never been read by this library. "No located record item contradicts" is doing positive work with those gaps open.

That a source-level likelihood ratio cannot be combined with other, non-DNA record evidence to yield an activity-level conclusion — the step evaluates the DNA in isolation from the toolmark, surveillance and attributed-statement material the 2026-09-01 ruling's identity analysis is recorded as resting on.

That the distinction between source-level and activity-level propositions is exhaustive for what a DNA result can bear, with no intermediate proposition (e.g. contact with an item at some unspecified time) that the results could support.

premises: §8.4 finding 3 states that the FBI analyst described a transfer mechanism.
§8.4 finding 3 states she did so on the State's own examination.
steps.conclusion: A route by which DNA can reach an item other than through the named person's own act with that item is affirmatively on the record, not merely a theoretical possibility.
implicit_premises: That the mechanism described applies to the items, quantities and mixture proportions at issue here. The document states no mechanism, no item it was described in relation to, and no testimony that it could account for these particular results.

That the phrase "on the State's own examination" carries evidential weight — it does so only if the State was examining a witness adverse to it, and §ES finding 3 records the opposite: both DNA analysts were defence witnesses, so the State's examination of each was the cross-examination, and it states in terms that this distinction is one the record does not support. §8.4 finding 3 still rests on the phrase; the §ES correction names that gap in another section without closing it here.

That a mechanism being available is enough to make it operative for these results — the step supplies nothing linking the described mechanism to the specific deposits, and none of the reported mixture proportions or degradation findings is brought to bear on whether it applies.

premises: The charging document's phrasing is "DNA on the trigger" (§10).

The trigger was swabbed together with the trigger guard, so the analyst could not say where within the swabbed area the DNA came from; that sample carried at least four contributors, possibly five, six or seven, with degradation, and the major profile was the most degraded (§8.2 caution 1).

The State argued "The defendant's DNA was found all over that gun. It was on the scope, the grips, the stock, and even the trigger," and the defence answered that what the analysts said was that there is evidentiary support for the inclusion of Tyler Robinson as a possible contributor (§ES finding 6).
§8.1 states that the interpretive connections asserted between the checkable anchors diverge from the record in one direction: toward source attribution.
steps.conclusion: Public and charging-layer restatements of these results assert propositions about source and about action that the laboratory results do not carry.
implicit_premises: That "DNA on the trigger" is being advanced and received as a claim about what Robinson did with the trigger, rather than as a claim about where a swab was taken — the step needs the activity reading for the restatement to be the error the chain names.

That the divergence running in one direction is a property of the population of restatements, not of the instances the file happens to hold. §10 records that this library holds very little media-narrative material about Robinson personally, so the direction claim rests on a small, non-surveyed set.

That the State's closing-argument characterisation and the charging document's phrasing are evidence of a general downstream pattern rather than two party-advocacy statements made under the rules of their own layer, which §ES finding 6 elsewhere treats as recording-layer material.

That the aggregation across locations in the State's sentence ("scope, grips, stock, trigger") adds nothing the per-item results do not, i.e. that a pattern across several locations cannot support an inference that no one location supports.

premises: The DNA results carry source-level propositions only.
Thirteen ATF items carry stated likelihood ratios naming Robinson on this record, plus two FBI figures (§8.2, §8.3).
Each of those items is subject to the same limitation: no analyst can say what action deposited the DNA, or when.
§8.1 states the forensic evidence naming Robinson is substantial in volume and narrow in what it can bear.
steps.conclusion: The volume of forensic material naming Robinson does not establish what he did — whose DNA it is cannot become what anyone did.
implicit_premises: That repetition across items adds no activity-level information, which requires the items' limitations to be perfectly correlated: that no pattern across trigger, bolt, barrel, scope, butt plate, fore-end, receiver underside, fired case, towel, screwdriver, Dremel buttons and etched cartridge case could support an activity inference that no single item supports.

That the conclusion, argued from DNA, holds for the forensic record as a whole. §8.1 states it of "the forensic evidence naming Robinson," but §8.6 carries firearms, toolmark and inscription material and §8.5 carries latent prints, and nothing here shows those are subject to the same activity/timing limitation.

That §8.1's still-current "unqualified and unrebutted by anyone" and "the most consistent proposition in the entire body of evidence" may carry the general conclusion, although §ES finding 3 withdrew the first as too strong and the second as a corpus-wide ranking no banked artifact can support and this file is not positioned to make.

That being narrow in what it can bear is a property of the evidence rather than of the propositions this file chose to test it against — no alternative proposition the volume could establish (e.g. repeated contact with the rifle) is stated and ruled out.

chain_name: The contributor count is an analyst input, not a measurement, and it is entangled with the same assumption
section: §8.4 finding 2, entangled with §8.4 finding 1; supporting material at §8.3 (FBI items 7 and 8), §9 item 2, §15 P8 row 10, §16 SINK
changed_since: Finding 2's own two sentences are unchanged and carry no correction marker. What has grown around it is its partner, finding 1, which now records at equal weight the examiner's recognised-practice answers ("Elimination samples are different… I can assume they're there… which is what I did here"; "I did not ignore it"), the magnitude exchange ("doesn't change the likelihood ratio of that major contributor by much" / "But it does change it, correct?" / "Yes", flagged as opening "It depends" and as scoped to a major contributor), the 2026-09-14 re-run of the scoped negative searches across all five hearing days plus the 09-01 argument, the express preference of "appears anywhere on this record" over "was ever computed," the unread State's Exhibit 31 and ≥379-page FBI case file, the PROVISIONAL flag on `DNA-E01` §3, and the "carry, don't resolve" disposition for D-53. Those hedges narrow what may be concluded from the chain, but they sit in finding 1 — finding 2 still asserts the count is subjective and not independent of the elimination donor, and the magnitude question the recorded exchange raises against it is not addressed where the claim is made. §15 P8 row 10 newly banks the 3 → 2 amendment as `SUPPORTED` alongside the 1.7 octillion ratio.

premises: The number of contributors to a DNA mixture is determined by the examiner.
That number is entered into the interpretation software as an input.
§8.4 finding 2 labels this a subjective determination and the examiner's own call.
steps.conclusion: The contributor count used in the reported calculations is an analyst's judgement supplied to the software, not a quantity the instrument measures.
implicit_premises: That the proposition, sourced from the FBI examiner's testimony about her own items, holds for contributor counts generally — including the ATF counts the file relies on elsewhere (item 1.3's "at least four contributors, possibly five, six or seven"; item 1.1's four-person mixture with two major contributors). No ATF testimony to this effect is cited at this finding.

That "analyst judgement" and "measurement" are exclusive categories — the step assumes a determination made under laboratory protocol from observed electropherogram data does not count as a measurement.

That being an analyst input is itself a limitation on what the figure can bear, rather than the ordinary and protocol-sanctioned method of mixture interpretation. §8.4 finding 1 records in terms that whether a likelihood ratio of 1 for an elimination donor is ordinary or anomalous practice is a technical question this library has NOT verified, and that the defence never established that assuming an elimination contributor is improper rather than routine.

premises: On FBI item 7, the towel, the contributor count moved from three to two.
§15's P8 rebuild records that amendment as `SUPPORTED` and records the associated ratio as 1.7 octillion.
§8.3 records FBI item 7 as a full profile, two contributors, one of whom is Twiggs, proportions 5% / 95%, with Robinson's profile "aligned better with the 95% contributor."
steps.conclusion: The contributor count behind the reported figure on FBI item 7 is a value that was changed, not the first value the examiner reached.
implicit_premises: That the reported 1.7 octillion figure was computed on the two-contributor call rather than the three — §15 records the amendment and the ratio side by side without stating which count produced the figure.
That the change ran from three to two for reasons bearing on the argument, rather than being a correction of a recording error or a re-read of the data on grounds unrelated to Twiggs.
That a changed input is more suspect than an unchanged one, i.e. that amendment indicates instability rather than ordinary review.

premises: The examiner testified that where an individual is submitted as an elimination sample she can assume that person is present, and that this is what she did here.
The two FBI figures are ratios between hypotheses that both place Twiggs among exactly two contributors, so the statistic never tests whether Twiggs is present (§8.4 finding 1).
§8.4 finding 2 states the two-person call is not independent of the elimination donor's introduction.
The conditioning is stated affirmatively on the record: "when I calculated the statistic for Mr. Robinson, I used Mr. Twiggs as an elimination."
steps.conclusion: The contributor count on FBI item 7 rests on the same elimination assumption that the conditioning problem identifies.
implicit_premises: That the dependence runs from the elimination assumption to the count. "Not independent of" is symmetric; the argument uses it in one direction only — as the assumption driving the count — and no record basis for that direction is stated.

That what the examiner described as her general handling of elimination samples is what determined item 7's count specifically; her quoted answer is about elimination samples as a class, with "which is what I did here" carrying the transfer.

That assuming a submitted elimination donor is present is an assumption capable of distorting the count, rather than the profession's ordinary handling of elimination samples — which §8.4 finding 1 records as a technical question this library has NOT verified and on which the record is unrebutted rather than settled.
That the same entanglement carries to FBI item 8, the screwdriver (also two contributors, one of whom is Twiggs), and to the ATF items, although the finding's only worked instance is item 7.

premises: The contributor count is an analyst input rather than a measured value.
That input is not independent of the elimination assumption.
The conditioning problem already means the statistic never tests whether Twiggs is present.
steps.conclusion: The contributor count supplies no independent check on the conditioning problem, so the two limitations compound rather than offsetting each other.
implicit_premises: That the reported likelihood ratio is materially sensitive to the contributor-count input. No magnitude is stated anywhere in the chain, and the only magnitude evidence on the record runs the other way: the examiner's unrebutted answer that for a major contributor the three-to-two change "doesn't change the likelihood ratio of that major contributor by much," with her agreement that it does change it.

That the scoped concession does not dispose of the point for the figure at issue — yet §8.3 records Robinson as aligned with the 95% (major) component of item 7, which would put the examiner's major-contributor answer directly on the figure this step concerns. The document flags her answer as opening "It depends" and as scoped to a major contributor without saying whether item 7's Robinson figure falls inside that scope.
That two limitations traceable to one assumption compound, rather than being a single limitation described twice.
That no other feature of the item constrains the count independently of the elimination assumption — no peak-height, stutter or allele-count evidence is brought to bear either way.

premises: No recalculation of Robinson's figure without the elimination assumption appears anywhere in the banked transcripts; all 24 likelihood-ratio passages were opened and read, and the counterfactual request forms return zero across the Bakker examination and across day1, day3, day4, day5 and the 2026-09-01 argument.
State's Exhibit 31 and the ≥379-page FBI case file are not banked and have never been read, so the null is scoped to the transcripts.
The examiner's account of her practice is unrebutted on this record, and the document states that unrebutted is not the same as verified.
D-53 is recorded as a property to be carried, not a conflict to be resolved; D-54 carries the contributor-count point.
steps.conclusion: The record is silent on the direction and size of any effect the elimination assumption had on the reported figures, and the contributor-count point is carried as a property of the evidence rather than resolved.
implicit_premises: That silence in the transcripts bounds what can be said about the figures' reliability. The document marks the limit by preferring "appears anywhere on this record" to "was ever computed," yet the finding is then used as a constraint on what the figures can bear — which is positive work for a scoped null.
That the unread Exhibit 31 and FBI case file would not contain the recalculation or the count's basis, or that their containing it would not change the conclusion.

That "carried, not resolved" is the correct resting place, rather than an open question whose answer would determine whether there is a limitation at all — the document says the practice question has not been verified and simultaneously treats the count's subjectivity as an established structural finding.

That D-54 supports the claim although its support runs through the project's own files: it was opened in `CR-E06` §7 and is carried by `DNA-E01`, whose §3 is flagged PROVISIONAL and has never been cleared by a verification cycle. The step's authority is the library's restatement, not a primary artifact.

That the examiner's recorded justification, marked "recorded, not adopted," leaves the objection standing — i.e. that declining to adopt her account is equivalent to the account not answering the objection.

chain_name: Consumption forecloses re-testing — and the count is scoped to one report
section: §8.4 finding 4 ("Consumption forecloses re-testing"), with the compressed restatement at §ES finding 7 and the supporting table and cautions at §8.2; register rows at §15 item 8 and §15 ("Consumption status of ATF items 15.1 and 18.1")
changed_since: The plainer earlier form asserted a bare "six of eleven ATF items were consumed" as a global fact and attributed both the consumed and the retained lists to the witness ("Oliver's list" — the document itself now says an earlier form of the parenthesis did this). The current form adds three things: (1) an attribution split — the consumed list is the witness's own unaided answer, the retained list is counsel's recitation carried by a one-word "Correct."; (2) an explicit Medium-high grade with its reason stated (both halves arrive through witnesses reading an exhibit the library has never read); (3) a scope guard — the eleven-item denominator belongs to State's Exhibit 30 alone, thirteen ATF items carry stated ratios across the record, and the consumption status of the two Exhibit 33 items (15.1, 18.1) is declared not on this record and separately registered as UNVERIFIED. §ES finding 7 was widened to carry the same scope caveat rather than the bare count.

premises: FBI items 1 through 6, the six swabs from the north-east corner of the Losee building, were entirely consumed and yielded no DNA at all.
FBI item 54, swabs of swiped finger areas, was entirely consumed and no result for it was ever stated on the record.
FBI item 55, two stairwell-railing swabs combined into one sample, produced a report of more than five individuals and no conclusion.
steps.conclusion: Those FBI samples are gone and produced nothing usable, so no further examination of them is possible.
implicit_premises: "Entirely consumed" means no physical material of any kind survives — not merely that the swab was used up, but that no extract, extraction residue or retained aliquot remains that a second laboratory could work from.
Consumption is the only barrier that matters: no retained electronic data (raw electropherograms, software files) exists that could be re-interpreted even where the physical sample is gone.
The witness testimony describing these items as consumed is accurate, and the machine transcript rendered the item designators correctly.
Re-testing would otherwise have been legally and practically available to some party, so that its unavailability is a loss rather than a non-event.

A sample that yielded no DNA at all is a meaningful loss to re-testing in the same way a sample that yielded a profile is — i.e. the foreclosure is worth reporting even where nothing was there to re-test.

premises: The ATF witness, answering without prompting, listed the consumed exhibits as 1.4, 1.6, 1.9, 1.10, 1.12, 2.1, 3.1, 4.1 and 5.1.
The Day-4 calculation table sets out eleven ATF items from State's Exhibit 30 that carry a stated likelihood ratio naming Robinson.
Six of the nine items on the witness's consumed list (1.4, 1.6, 1.9, 2.1, 3.1, 5.1) are among those eleven.
steps.conclusion: Six of the eleven ATF items carrying stated likelihood ratios in State's Exhibit 30 were entirely consumed.
implicit_premises: The item designators used in the Day-5 consumption answer refer to the same physical items as the identically numbered designators in the Day-4 calculation table — no renumbering between exhibits, days or laboratories.
The witness's recited consumed list is complete: no consumed ratio-bearing item was omitted from her answer.
The three listed items that are not in the ratio table (1.10, 1.12, 4.1) genuinely carry no stated ratio, rather than carrying one that was simply never read aloud.
The Day-4 table, which reaches the library only through a non-expert officer reading aloud from an exhibit the library has never read, correctly identifies which items bear ratios.
"Consumed" in the witness's list carries the same meaning as the disposition column of the table.

premises: Recomputed on 2026-09-14: six consumed plus five retained equals eleven.
The consumed set and the retained set share no member.
No ratio-bearing item is left unaccounted for by the two sets.
steps.conclusion: The partition of the eleven Exhibit 30 items into consumed and retained is arithmetically complete and internally consistent, and the count is marked SUPPORTED.
implicit_premises: Every ratio-bearing item has exactly one of two dispositions: there is no third status such as partially consumed, lost, mis-inventoried, or transferred to another laboratory.
Arithmetic consistency of the file's own bookkeeping is evidence about the real disposition of the physical items, not merely evidence that the file adds up.
The five-item retained list, which is counsel's recitation of page 8 assented to by the witness with a single word, reports that page accurately.
Page 8 of State's Exhibit 30 is a complete disposition record for the eleven items, so a partition derived from it cannot be missing an item.

premises: Both halves of the join reach this library only through witnesses reading aloud from an exhibit the library has never itself read.
The retained half is counsel's reading of the page, assented to by the witness, rather than the witness's own recitation.
The consumed half is the witness's own unaided answer.
steps.conclusion: The six-of-eleven join is graded Medium-high rather than High.
implicit_premises: Transmission through a read-aloud exhibit that the library has never inspected caps confidence at Medium-high — and also floors it there, i.e. this defect is not severe enough to drop the grade to Medium or below.
A one-word assent to counsel's recitation is reliable enough to sustain a Medium-high grade on the retained half.
The Rev machine transcript rendered the strings of item numbers accurately, even though numbers are the class of token the file's own caveats treat as most vulnerable to machine-transcript error.
The two halves, differently attested, can be combined into one grade rather than each carrying its own.
The grade is a calibrated output of a verification act by this project rather than a convention applied to second-hand material generally.

premises: Two further ATF items, 15.1 (swabs of the Dremel's buttons) and 18.1 (swabs of the etched "test shot" .30-06 cartridge case), carry stated likelihood ratios naming Robinson that were read into the record.
Those two come from a different report, State's Exhibit 33, the ATF forensic-biology report on the Dremel and the home cartridge cases.
Counting them with the eleven from Exhibit 30 gives thirteen ATF items carrying stated ratios across the whole record.
steps.conclusion: The eleven-item denominator belongs to State's Exhibit 30 alone; the count may not be written as a record-wide figure.
implicit_premises: The two Exhibit 33 items are items of the same kind as the eleven — comparable ratio-bearing items whose consumption status would be a comparable fact — so their existence genuinely changes the denominator.

"Thirteen" is itself only a count of what was read aloud, not of what the exhibits contain; the file states this elsewhere (Exhibit 33 was walked through for at least five numbered calculations and counsel declined to have the rest read), so "thirteen across this record" is a floor and the denominator is in fact unknown.
The number-to-location mapping for 15.1 and 18.1, which rests on one officer's Day-4 reading, is correct.
A denominator being a floor rather than a known total does not prevent the scoping guard from doing its work.

premises: Page 8 of State's Exhibit 30, the source of the consumed/retained split, does not cover the 15.x or 18.x series.
A search of day4.txt for the stem "consum" returns zero hits under both readings of the U+FFFE line-break split.
A search of day5.txt for the strings "15.1" and "18.1" returns zero hits.
steps.conclusion: The consumption status of ATF items 15.1 and 18.1 is not on this record at all, which is not the same as saying they were retained.
implicit_premises: The searched corpus — page 8 as reported, day4.txt and day5.txt — is coextensive with "this record", so material absent from it is absent from the record.

If consumption of those items had been discussed, the word would have used the stem "consum"; no paraphrase ("used up", "nothing left", "depleted", "no sample remaining", "we don't have any more") could have conveyed it, since none was searched.
The item numbers would appear in the transcript in the literal digit form "15.1"/"18.1" rather than spelled out, split, or garbled by the machine transcription.
Running the search under both U+FFFE readings removes every known false-null hazard for this corpus, leaving zero hits as genuine absence rather than a search artifact.

The library's never having read the face of Exhibit 33 does not bear on whether the status is "on the record", i.e. the exhibit's own content is outside what "this record" means here even though the exhibit was in evidence.

premises: The named FBI samples are gone and produced nothing usable (S1).
Six of the eleven Exhibit 30 ratio-bearing items were entirely consumed, at Medium-high, scoped to that one report (S2–S6).
Elimination samples from the investigators were requested and were not received.
steps.conclusion: Consumption has foreclosed re-testing, and the six-of-eleven count is a scoped figure that may not be written globally.
implicit_premises: Non-receipt of investigator elimination samples belongs to the same finding as sample consumption — i.e. both are instances of one foreclosure — rather than being a separate fact about investigative completeness.
"Requested and not received" is itself established on this record at the confidence the sentence implies.

The headline "consumption forecloses re-testing" remains accurate notwithstanding that five of the eleven Exhibit 30 items were retained and remain re-testable; the claim is about the consumed subset, not about the body of DNA evidence as a whole.
Foreclosure of re-testing is a fact about the evidence rather than a suggestion about the reliability of the results that were obtained before consumption.

chain_name: The guard that runs the other way: from a corpus silence to a High-confidence null about inflation
section: §8.4 finding 1 ("The conditioning problem") — the closing guard of the finding, ending "Confidence: High that the record is silent on the direction and size of any effect. This guard may not be softened, buried, or written in a way that implies its opposite."
changed_since: The plainer earlier form asserted the null unscoped. The current text adds the explicit correction that this is "a scoped null about the TRANSCRIPT, not a claim about what the FBI laboratory did or did not calculate", names "appears anywhere on this record" as the correct form and "was ever computed" as the overclaim, and records that State's Exhibit 31 and the FBI case file of 379-plus pages are unbanked and unread. It also adds: the 2026-09-14 re-run of the stem search under both U+FFFE readings and over five further transcripts; a phase-label flag withdrawing "on redirect" as inherited rather than primary; the statement that the main clause stays second-hand/analyst and is not repointed; the note that the examiner's account is "unrebutted on this record — which is not the same as verified"; and the disposition that D-53 is a property to be carried rather than a conflict to resolve.

premises: The two FBI likelihood ratios are ratios between two hypotheses that both place Lance Twiggs among exactly two contributors.
The examiner stated affirmatively that when she calculated the statistic for Robinson she used Twiggs as an elimination.
steps.conclusion: The statistic never tests whether Twiggs is in fact present.
implicit_premises: A likelihood ratio between two hypotheses that share an assumption can carry no information about that shared assumption.
The transcript's rendering of the two competing hypotheses is accurate and complete.
These two figures are the only FBI figures at issue, so what is true of them is true of the FBI statistical evidence naming Robinson.

premises: A purposive negative search of the full Bakker examination in day2.txt, re-run on 2026-09-14 with artifact_search.py under both readings of the U+FFFE split, returns zero hits for the stems "inflat", "exaggerat" and "overstat".
All 24 passages in that examination matching "likelihood rat*" were opened and read, and none states a Robinson figure computed without the Twiggs assumption.

Zero counterfactual request forms appear anywhere in the examination — "what would", "if you had not", "without the assumption", "recalculat", "re-run", "had you not", "absent", "hypothetical" — the one "if you didn't" hit being about sample consumption rather than the ratio.
The same search returns the same null over day1.txt, day3.txt, day4.txt, day5.txt and the 2026-09-01 final argument transcript.
The same three stems return zero hits over day2_condensed.txt as well as day2.txt.
steps.conclusion: No passage in the banked transcripts asserts that the elimination assumption inflated, exaggerated or overstated the Robinson figure, and no figure computed without that assumption appears anywhere in them.
implicit_premises: The three stems and the eight enumerated counterfactual forms exhaust the ways counsel or a witness could have raised the point — no unsearched wording ("higher than it should be", "biased upward", "skewed", "too strong", "overestimate", "favourable", "conservative", "boost") could carry the same content.

Reading the 24 "likelihood rat*" passages covers every place in the examination where an unconditioned Robinson figure could have appeared — such a figure could not have been given in a passage that does not use that phrase.
The machine transcript would have rendered any such word correctly had it been spoken; a garbled or mis-transcribed instance would not be silently absent from a stem search.
Searching under both U+FFFE readings removes every known false-null hazard for this corpus, so zero hits means absence and not method failure.
The banked transcripts are complete renderings of everything said on those days.

premises: The scope of that null is the transcripts.
State's Exhibit 31 and the FBI case file of at least 379 pages are not banked and have never been read by this library.
steps.conclusion: The correct form of the claim is that nothing of the kind appears anywhere on this record; "was ever computed" would overclaim, because the null is about the transcript and not about what the FBI laboratory did.
implicit_premises: A null scoped to the transcripts is nonetheless the relevant null for the finding this file is making — i.e. what the record shows is the question, not what the laboratory did.

The unread Exhibit 31 and FBI case file could contain exactly the material the null excludes, and that live possibility is compatible with grading the transcript-scoped null at High rather than lowering it.
The distinction between "on this record" and "was ever computed" is one downstream readers will preserve, so the scoped form does not function in practice as the unscoped one.

premises: The examiner's answer on magnitude, which nobody rebutted, was that for a major contributor the change from three contributors to two "doesn't change the likelihood ratio of that major contributor by much".
Asked "But it does change it, correct?", she answered "Yes".
Her answer opens with "It depends", and the concession is scoped to a major contributor.
steps.conclusion: The only on-record statement about the size of any effect is hedged and scoped, and states that a change occurs without stating its direction or its magnitude.
implicit_premises: "Doesn't change it by much" is not a statement of size, even though it is an ordinal claim about size — i.e. a vague magnitude claim counts as no magnitude claim for the purposes of the null.
"It does change it — Yes" is not a statement of direction, so an acknowledged change with no stated sign leaves the record silent on direction.

steps.step: S1 — From executed searches to an inventory of biographical nulls
premises: Searches were run across the whole corpus — all topic folders, all evidence files, all acquisition logs — for a list of biographical categories about Robinson.

For Robinson's own religious affiliation, the corpus yields nothing at Tier 1 or Tier 2.

For social-media presence, writings or documents authored by him, the corpus yields nothing beyond the handwritten note, the messages quoted in the charging documents, and the Discord thread admitted as State's Exhibit 16.2; a re-run across fourteen named platforms surfaced no second platform, handle, account or posting history attributed to him.

It is not a claim that no such material exists in the world.
It is not a claim that any of these things is true or false of Robinson.

The project's standing rule is that a search null is a claim about the search, not about the world, and that absence of evidence is evidence of absence only where the search space would necessarily contain the record.

Presenting the item as the first of "the seven findings that matter most" and as a headlined finding in its own right carries no implicature beyond its literal scope — that is, a null can be foregrounded as a finding without functioning as a positive claim.

implicit_premises: That the ATF designator '18A–18E' maps onto the five casings a witness separately described as being atop the safe; the passage asserts the join but the join is between a report designator and a spoken description, made by the same non-examiner witness.

steps.step: S3 — Exhibit 33 puts DNA figures naming Robinson on two items inside that chain
premises: State's Exhibit 33 is an ATF forensic-biology report on the Dremel tool and the cartridge cases found in the home.

Faumuina read that ATF item 15.1, swabs of the Dremel's buttons, is at least one trillion times more likely if it originated from Tyler Robinson as a contributor to the major component and two unknown individuals than from three unknown individuals.
She read the same formulation for ATF item 18.1, the etched 'test shot' .30-06 case from atop the safe, except 'as a major component'.

steps.step: S4 — The figures are capped, not measured
premises: §8.2's caution 3 states that 'at least one trillion' is a reporting cap, not a measurement.
Both the 15.1 and the 18.1 figures are in the capped form.
§ES finding 4 adds that a cap conceals how large a ratio is, not how small, so above the cap the magnitude is unrecoverable.

That the banked .txt transcripts exhaust the record for this purpose, and that transcription of a spoken decimal designator into text is reliable.
That single-sourcing here is a defect of this record rather than the ordinary situation of a document read into evidence once.

premises: Asked what was tested, the witness answered 'The Dremel tool, the bits' container, as well as the cartridges and cartridge casings we found in Tyler's home.'

That counsel's decision not to have paragraphs read means the paragraphs exist and contain calculations.

premises: Exhibit 34 identified Exhibit 15A, the longest metal bit, as the tool that made the marks.
The DNA swab of the longest metal bit is ATF item 15.5.
No ratio for 15.5 was ever read into the record.
The Dremel figure that was read is 15.1, the buttons.

steps.step: S9 — The counterweight travels in the same breath
premises: ATF item 15.1, the same Dremel-button swab, also carries support for inclusion of Lance Twiggs.
The rifle's bolt and barrel, ATF items 1.4 and 1.6, carry support for inclusion of Matthew Robinson.
The ATF analyst stated that it is reasonable to assume anyone living in the household could have contributed DNA to an object found in that household.

steps.conclusion: A description of the convergence that omits these results overstates it.
implicit_premises: That 'support for inclusion' results and capped likelihood ratios are commensurable enough that omitting the former distorts the latter — the two are different statistical statements and the file does not say what the Twiggs support-for-inclusion value was.
That the presence of a second contributor's DNA on the same swab weakens the inference drawn from the first — an assumption about mixture interpretation that no cited testimony states.

That 'overstates' is a claim about how a chain must be WRITTEN (a project norm) rather than a claim about what the evidence shows; the step's conclusion is normative while its premises are evidentiary.

That the household-transfer framing genuinely does not extend to the rifle swabs, i.e. that the rifle is relevantly unlike a household object for transfer purposes — asserted as a scope limit, never argued.
